content:
The owner of the Bichon Frise named Weiwei, who was killed by a dog bite, posted a悼念 message on social media today. The owner said Weiwei enjoyed going out for walks, twice a day. Yesterday, during a walk at the pet park, a large dog about half a person's height suddenly rushed out and bit Weiwei on the neck.

The owner recalled trying various methods, including kicking the large dog, spraying water at its nose, and using treats to distract it, but the large dog held on tightly and refused to let go. The owner said: 'I screamed for help and was grateful for the kind passers-by who assisted, but facing a large dog weighing tens of pounds that would not release its grip, everyone was helpless. I could only watch helplessly as my little dog lost her life.'

Weiwei died on the spot. The owner recalled that the large dog remained guarding Weiwei's body until police arrived and restrained it, after which the owner was able to recover the remains. 'I later learned that the vicious dog had also killed another small dog. From beginning to end, the owner of the large dog never appeared.'

The owner said the family was deeply grieved by the sudden tragedy and had difficulty sleeping through the night. 'Weiwei was an exceptionally well-behaved and gentle little dog, our whole family's little angel. I really want to hold her and kiss her again. I cannot believe she has suddenly left us just like that.' The owner uploaded the last video of Weiwei before the incident, showing Weiwei sitting in a stroller, being well-behaved and adorable in a shopping mall. The owner said: 'Only by repeatedly watching her curious and adorable appearance can I temporarily forget the horrible scene.'

The Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) said in response to media enquiries yesterday that after inspection, the dog involved in biting the dog to death had a microchip and a valid dog licence. The Department will contact the owner based on the information on the dog's licence, and will investigate the incident. If there is sufficient evidence, prosecution will be initiated.

The AFCD pointed out that dog owners must always keep their dogs under proper control, including securely leashing large dogs, to prevent causing nuisance or harm to other people or animals. According to the Rabies Ordinance, dogs must be leashed or otherwise properly controlled when in public places, or in other places where it can reasonably be expected that the dog will wander into a public place. Offenders may be fined HK$10,000.

The Collective is asking the AFCD whether the dog owner has been contacted today, and is awaiting a reply.
